analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds a short paragraph at head lines ~1293-1298 about PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup. The paragraph says all of a request's hits are snapshotted before promotion between the two bounded generations, so a rotation cannot turn later pieces into misses. It also says token arrays share storage during the snapshot, existing admission and byte bounds still apply, and batches with no old-generation hits skip the promotion pass. The supplied units (head lines 1612-2426) are unchanged surrounding documentation. I reviewed them and saw no new security-relevant claims: no endpoint, auth, attestation, encryption, key-handling, or cache-storage changes.

Possible threat-model interaction: the piece-token store is described as scoped to the prefix-cache scope, which is coordinator-authored per account. T-041 and SEC-035 cover the same-account TTFT oracle. The doc change is correctness and performance (avoiding spurious misses), and it reiterates that existing bounds still apply. Cross-scope isolation of the in-memory piece store is documented as pre-existing. Because the source code is not in this batch, I cannot confirm that the snapshot logic keeps scope isolation or the byte bounds. If the code changes the lookup key or shares token arrays across scopes, that is a question for the code-change review pass, not a documentation finding. No threat-model update is needed from the doc text alone. No findings.
